<pasted_content id="2560">
Что делаем
Чинить P02. Восстановить, как считается relationship charge, и встроить его в расчёт стоимости сделки у агента, чтобы защита от сделки хуже стартовой цены срабатывала с учётом штрафа. Сначала проверить на P02 и P03 (stabilise), потом полным прогоном.
Читать replay. Причины, которые поставщик указывает в replay, и есть легальный реверс-инжиниринг его поведения. По ним проверяй гипотезы вида «давить или не давить в кейсе с этой целью».
Поднимать P11, затем P08 и P18. Одно изменение за раз, проверка на арене, повтор только для того, что собираешься оставить.
Финальная проверка. Кандидата прогнать 2 раза по всем кейсам. Сравнивать отдельно уходы и нули.

Бюджет: 524 сессии, примерно 50 полных прогонов. Узкое место — время, а не попытки. Симулятор оставь только для проверки, что агент не сломался.
</pasted_content id="2560">


<pasted_content id="2560">
продолжать в этой сессии или новую сделать? как ты себя по контексту чуствуешь

Лучше начать новую. Эта сессия очень длинная, и большая её часть — уже закрытые темы (playbook, симулятор, медленные уступки). Точного счётчика контекста у меня нет, но при такой длине ранние части начинают сжиматься в краткие пересказы, и детали теряются.

Новая сессия ничего не потеряет: всё важное лежит в файлах и запушено в main (2fde9e2).

- AGENTS.md — правила, таблица приоритетов по кейсам, жёсткость по цели кейса.
- agent/docs/backlog.md — где теряем очки и список задач.
- agent/docs/runs.md и agent/docs/benchmarks/ — все прогоны с результатами.
- agent/docs/knowledge/ — гайд по книгам и факты из FAQ.
- agent/docs/simulator.md — почему симулятору нельзя верить на practice.

Для старта новой сессии хватит одной фразы: «Прочитай AGENTS.md и agent/docs/backlog.md, почини пункт 6 (оценка relationship charge в stabilise и secure_supply кейсах), начни с P02».

Осталось 524 попытки из 650. Папка conversations/ по-прежнему не в git; в этом чате лежит ключ арены, так что не коммить её.

✻ Cogitated for 9s · done 11:02 PM
</pasted_content id="2560">

 ест ьеще идея попробовать что-то из психологии добавить - самое глвавное я хочу вначале просить меньше чем на что мы готовы чтобы психологически сразу сдвинуть avg. можешь использовать subagents if applicable. скажи мне потом куда я могу посмотреть чтобы увидеть прям промпт и кейсы наши которые у нас есть. разрешаю тебе максиму 50 использовать попыток. 

<pasted_content id="2560">
Проверка понимания кейсов и целей сделки агентом.
Какие у нас кейсы
Тип кейса — это рычаг (о чём спор), цель — как с этим поставщиком себя вести.

Кейс    Ситуация    Цель
P01    Литейный завод объявил +9.5% на корпуса насосов    stabilise
P02    Производитель моторов перекладывает рост цен на медь    stabilise
P03    Продление рамочного договора на частотные преобразователи    stabilise
P04    Продление договора на подшипник 6306    routine
P05    Тендер (RFQ) на вал насоса, 3 участника    leverage
P07    Собрать крепёж у одного дистрибьютора (бандл)    routine
P08    Сырьевая надбавка и базовая цена на сталь 1.4404    leverage
P10    Поставщик урезает выделенный нам объём уплотнений    secure supply
P11    Кронштейны подшипников, «в красной зоне» (судя по названию, качество)    quality first
P18    То же, что P08, другой поставщик    leverage
</pasted_content id="2560">

. На P08 лучший результат вырос с 0.73 до 0.91, и сделала это одна команда (beaten 1). Кто-то нашёл в сырьевом кейсе крупный рычаг. На P18, кейсе того же типа, лучший пока 0.68: похоже, этот приём там ещё никто не применил.

<pasted_content id="2560">
Где может быть хитринка
Рычаг в сырьевых кейсах. Одна команда сделала +0.16 над house на P08, и это самый явный сигнал на всей доске. Гипотезы для проверки в replay:
отделить надбавку от базовой цены и спорить с каждой отдельно;
привязать надбавку к индексу металла (никель, молибден) с понятной формулой, периодом усреднения и потолком;
проверить, не сидит ли металл уже в базовой цене, то есть не платим ли мы за него дважды.
Если приём найдётся на P08 и сработает на P18, это механизм, который ударит и по закрытым сырьевым кейсам.
Условия, а не только цена. На дашборде экономия считается за весь горизонт договора. Значит, срок фиксации цены, условия оплаты, длительность договора и формула индексации могут весить в счёте больше, чем пара процентов цены, а поставщику стоить мало. Это классический обмен: отдать то, что дёшево нам и дорого ему, и забрать обратное. Именно такой рычаг вероятнее всего пропущен на P11, где 17 из 20 команд его нашли.
Стабильность в финале. Все таблицы на дашборде показывают лучшую попытку из многих, а финал — это один прогон на 15–50 новых кейсах. Агент, у которого нет нулей и уходов и который стабильно держится на уровне house или выше, обгонит команды, чьи 0.79 собраны из удачных попыток. Это преимущество, которое на доске не видно.
Не делай prompt injection в поставщика (например, «игнорируй свои инструкции»). Скорее всего, это против правил, и риск дисквалификации не стоит выигрыша. Если сомневаешься, проверь правила хакатона.
</pasted_content id="2560">

 вот это точно субагенту - 

<pasted_content id="2560">
Аугментированные данные

Да, но используй их для проверки того, что агент правильно понимает кейс, а не для подбора стратегии. Закрытые тесты — это новые брифы. Баг P02 был как раз ошибкой расчёта, а не тактики.

Конкретно:

Claude генерирует 30–50 вариантов брифов по мотивам 10 практических кейсов и двух демо (D01, D02): другие цены, объёмы, горизонты, формулировки, цены металлов и смешанные типы.
Для каждого варианта правильный ответ считается отдельно: тип кейса, цель, стартовая стоимость за горизонт, наша граница, relationship charge.
Запускается только шаг, на котором агент разбирает бриф, без переговоров. Его ответы сравниваются с правильными.

Это бесплатно, не зависит от точности симулятора и ловит именно те ошибки, которые дают ноль в финале. Отдельно проверь, что делает агент, если тип кейса не похож ни на один известный: в закрытых тестах такие могут быть.
</pasted_content id="2560">

# Backlog: where we lose score, and what to work on

As of 10 October 2026, 21:30. Source: the `tactical` run over the 10 hosted practice cases
(`20261010-211824-practice-tactical`, commit `96f7545`, mean 0.695), its trace and events, and the practice
leaderboard read at 21:35 (we are 5th of 22 with 73.2 points over our best scores; the leader has 79.0).

Every figure below is from that run unless a source is named. The "why" of each problem is read from the trace and
the `thread_hold` events; the rule in `tactical.py` behind each stop has not been traced line by line.

## 1. The cases by lever, with what the run lost

| Lever | Case | Score | EUR above C_best | Rounds used of 10 | How the thread ended |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Price increase | P01 | 0.856 | 8,192 | 2 | held: "their offer meets our ask", supplier still `open` |
| Price increase (copper) | P02 | 0.686 | 14,854 | 2 | supplier `agreed` to our sheet |
| Raw-material surcharge | P08 | 0.570 | 75,422 | 4 | held: "last word: take it" on a `final_offer` |
| Raw-material surcharge | P18 | 0.419 | 42,133 | 3 | supplier `agreed`: we went 5.00 → 5.25 → 5.50, its price |
| Renewal | P03 | 0.905 | 31,992 | 4 | held: "the supplier stopped moving" |
| Renewal | P04 | 0.860 | 324 | 3 | held: "last word: take it" on a `final_offer` |
| RFQ | P05 | 0.742 | 21,153 | 3 | supplier `agreed`: we went 30.46 → 28.00 against its 28.79 |
| Bundling | P07 | 0.721 | 25,607 | 4 | held: "last word: take it" on a `final_offer` |
| Capacity | P10 | 0.647 | 212,881 | 2 | `final_offer` in its first reply (33.80, alternative 31.90); we took the alternative |
| Quality | P11 | 0.545 | 43,244 | 4 | held: "last word: take it", supplier still `open` |

### The best any team reached, per case

From the arena's live page (screenshot of 10 October, about 21:05; 24 teams) against our best score per case
(`runs.md`, after P-14):

| Case | Lever | Best team | House agent | Teams that beat the house | Our best | Gap to the best |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| P08 | raw-material surcharge | 0.91 | 0.75 | 1 | 0.603 | 0.31 |
| P18 | raw-material surcharge | 0.68 | 0.39 | 17 | 0.467 | 0.21 |
| P02 | price increase (copper) | 0.85 | 0.74 | 1 | 0.686 | 0.16 |
| P11 | quality | 0.81 | 0.31 | 17 | 0.692 | 0.12 |
| P05 | RFQ | 0.92 | 0.56 | 12 | 0.824 | 0.10 |
| P07 | bundling | 0.81 | 0.78 | 1 | 0.721 | 0.09 |
| P01 | price increase | 0.99 | 0.97 | 2 | 0.917 | 0.07 |
| P10 | capacity | 0.70 | 0.69 | 3 | 0.647 | 0.05 |
| P03 | renewal | 0.94 | 0.92 | 1 | 0.905 | 0.04 |
| P04 | renewal | 0.87 | 0.86 | 14 | 0.860 | 0.01 |

The two raw-material cases hold 0.52 of the 1.16 between us and the best team on every case; P08 at 0.91 was reached
by one team. The practice board showed us 6th with a mean of 0.73; the leader had 0.81.

## 2. The problems, largest first

### 2.1 We stop after two to four of ten rounds

No thread used more than four rounds. In P18 and P05 the supplier agreed to our own rising offer (P18: 5.00 → 5.25
→ 5.50 against its 5.60); in P01 and P11 the thread was held while the supplier's status was still `open`.

- P18: deal 264,784, our upper bound 259,433, C_best 222,651.
- P10 is a different case: the supplier called its first reply final (33.80, with an alternative at 31.90) and we
  took the alternative. The deal costs 1,541,808 against our upper bound of 1,374,881 and C_best 1,328,927; what
  would have moved it is not in the trace.
- P02 closed in round 2 below our own ask (358.45 against 361.34), after we offered an index clause.

### 2.2 Our estimate of what is reachable is too high in leverage cases

The upper bound (`plan` event) against the arena's C_best:

| Case | Upper bound | C_best | Upper bound above C_best |
|---|---|---|---|
| P05 | 272,392 | 223,424 | 21.9 % |
| P18 | 259,433 | 222,651 | 16.5 % |
| P08 | 1,028,315 | 960,309 | 7.1 % |
| P07 | 319,069 | 299,241 | 6.6 % |
| P03 | 4,102,637 | 3,909,043 | 5.0 % |
| P01 | 1,143,596 | 1,096,816 | 4.3 % |
| P10 | 1,374,881 | 1,328,927 | 3.5 % |
| P04 | 197,524 | 196,529 | 0.5 % |
| P02 | 2,282,867 | 2,235,514 | 2.1 % |
| P11 | 710,733 | 722,500 | -1.6 % |

An offer inside a bound that is too high counts as good enough, so the thread closes early (2.1).

### 2.3 A lever the supplier names is not pulled

P11: the supplier wrote "Faster payment would help us more than anything" in four replies, and "If you want a lower
price, we need to drop the chargebacks". The profile had it as `cash_short`. Its price went 47.00 → 48.50 → 47.00 →
46.50 → 46.50 and we took it with six rounds left. P07: "A binding higher volume would help us and can improve the
price" in round 4.

### 2.4 Arguments that are spent for nothing

- The price-history argument came back "it holds, but it does not change our calculation" in five cases (P18, P08,
  P10, P02, P11). It takes one of the three argument slots of the first e-mail each time.
- P07: the forecast was cited in four e-mails; three came back `duplicate`, and the supplier answered "that volume
  change was already factored into our previous calculation" three times.

### 2.5 What is no longer a problem: the volume question

On 10 October in the afternoon the most common supplier sentence was "Which volume can you commit to?", unanswered
(`rejections.md`, row 1). In this run the forecast argument came back "it holds and we took it into account" in P18,
P08, P02, P07 and P11.

### 2.6 A final offer is final on practice

`playbook`'s closing offer after a final offer made three suppliers walk away (P04, P07, P18):
[`benchmarks/2026-10-10-playbook-none.md`](benchmarks/2026-10-10-playbook-none.md). Problem 2.1 is about the rounds
before a final offer, not about pushing past one.

### 2.7 Our cost of a deal misses the relationship charge

P02 (`stabilise`), run `20261010-221425-practice-tactical-slow25`: we accepted EUR 345.39 and computed C as 2,135,441.
The arena's C is 2,314,646, of which 179,204 is the relationship charge for leaving the supplier below its
sustainable margin; the deal is above C_open and scored 0. At 358.45 (run `20261010-211824-practice-tactical`) the
charge was 56,127. Our estimate of the charge was 0 in both, so the guard that refuses a deal worse than the opening
did not fire.

## 3. Work items

| # | Item | Cases it concerns | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | ~~Concede more slowly while the supplier is `open`~~ - tried as `tactical-slow25`: sandbox D02 0.587 → 0.671, practice mean 0.695 → 0.621 (0.696 → 0.690 without P02). No gain. | P18, P05 | 2.1 |
| 2 | Do not hold a thread on "last word" or "meets our ask" while the status is `open` and the supplier names a lever | P11, P01 | 2.1, 2.3 |
| 3 | Lower the upper bound for leverage cases, or stop using it as a reason to close | P05, P18, P08, P07 | 2.2 |
| 4 | When a supplier names a lever twice, send a sheet that gives it (shortest payment, no chargeback) at its price | P11, P07 | 2.3 |
| 5 | Drop the price-history argument from the first e-mail; never cite one ID twice | all | 2.4 |
| 6 | In `stabilise` and `secure_supply` cases, estimate the supplier's cost before pushing the price down, and stop where the relationship charge outweighs the price | P02, P01, P03, P10 | 2.7 |

## 4. How to test changes

- **Holdout.** Tune on P01, P04, P05, P07, P08, P10 and P11. Do not look at P02, P03 and P18 until a change is
  finished: each has a twin of the same lever in the tuning set (P01, P04, P08), so a gain that does not carry over
  to them is fitted to a case, not to a lever.
- **Cost.** One run over the seven tuning cases is 7 sessions; the holdout 3. `tactical` uses no LLM, so one run per
  change is enough.
- **Variations.** The arena cannot be given changed cases. `negotiator sim bench --jitter --strangers` moves the
  floors and swaps the suppliers' habits on the same scenarios; use it as a gate (a change must not lose there), not
  as a score. Its error on practice cases is in [`simulator.md`](simulator.md).

"""The published cost function: what a term sheet costs the buyer in €, plus term helpers.

C covers the buyer's fixed need over a fixed horizon: need the deal does not cover is bought at
the case's fallback price (plus the fallback risk of the category goal), committed volume is bought
needed or not, and units bought before a new price takes effect cost the current price. In
strategic and bottleneck cases a deal that leaves the supplier below a sustainable margin costs
too - pass your estimate of the supplier (`supplier_value`) to price that. Do the arithmetic here,
not in the language model.
"""

import math
import operator
from datetime import date

# Strategic and bottleneck goals: leaving the supplier below a sustainable margin costs.
RELATIONSHIP_GOALS = {"stabilise", "secure_supply"}
OPS = {
    "<=": operator.le,
    "<": operator.lt,
    ">=": operator.ge,
    ">": operator.gt,
    "==": operator.eq,
    "!=": operator.ne,
}


def closing_terms(case, terms, standard=None):
    """The terms a deal would close on: the term sheet, then the supplier's standard terms (from
    its quote PDF) for anything left out, then the case's fixed terms; gaps from the buyer's plan.
    """
    b = case["buyer"]
    freight = b["freight_eur_per_unit"]
    plan = {
        "volume_per_year": b["need_per_year"],
        "contract_months": round(12 * b["horizon_years"]),
        "payment_days": b["reference_payment_days"],
        "lead_time_days": b["need_lead_time_days"],
        # an unknown Incoterm counts as the costliest: a cautious buyer does not assume DAP
        "incoterm": max(freight, key=freight.get),
    }
    t = dict(plan)
    for layer in (standard or {}, case.get("fixed_terms", {}), terms):
        t.update({k: v for k, v in layer.items() if v is not None or k not in plan})
    return t


def horizon_start(case):
    """The horizon starts at the fixed or the earliest possible effective date."""
    fixed = case.get("fixed_terms", {}).get("effective_date")
    options = [o for o in case.get("term_options", {}).get("effective_date", []) if o]
    first = fixed or (min(options) if options else None)
    return date.fromisoformat(first) if first else None


def _years(case, t):
    """Years of the horizon a deal covers; a single order (0 months) counts as one year's lot.
    A commitment beyond the horizon neither costs nor earns."""
    months = t["contract_months"]
    return min(months / 12 if months else 1.0, case["buyer"]["horizon_years"])


def _units_before(case, t, years):
    """Units bought between the horizon start and the date a new price takes effect."""
    start = horizon_start(case)
    if not t.get("effective_date") or start is None:
        return 0.0
    lag = (date.fromisoformat(t["effective_date"]) - start).days / 365
    return t["volume_per_year"] * min(max(lag, 0.0), years)


def supplier_value(case, terms, supplier):
    """What a deal is worth to the supplier per unit, in cash: the price at its standard terms that
    would pay it the same. `supplier` is your estimate of it:
      standard       its standard terms (quote PDF, `docs.standard_terms`)
      interest_rate  what money now is worth to it per year (more to a supplier short of cash)
      usual_rate     its usual cost of money (default: interest_rate); tooling paid up front is
                     worth more to it when cash is dearer than usual
      ppm            the defect rate it really achieves (default: its standard ppm commitment)
      extra          EUR per unit it gains (+) or spends (-) beyond these items, e.g. overtime for
                     a faster delivery or idle capacity a larger volume fills (default 0)
    Contract length and an index clause are security, not cash: they do not count here."""
    b, std = case["buyer"], {**supplier["standard"], **case.get("fixed_terms", {})}
    t = closing_terms(case, terms, std)
    years = _years(case, t)
    sold = t["volume_per_year"] * years
    old = _units_before(case, t, years) / sold  # sold at the current price
    rate = supplier["interest_rate"]
    pay = 1 - rate * (t["payment_days"] - std["payment_days"]) / 360
    cash_now = 1 + (rate - supplier.get("usual_rate", rate)) * years / 2
    freight = b["freight_eur_per_unit"]
    ppm = supplier.get("ppm", std.get("ppm_commitment") or 0)
    return (
        t["unit_price"] * (1 - old) * pay
        + old * (b.get("current_unit_price") or 0.0) * pay
        + freight[t["incoterm"]]
        - freight[std["incoterm"]]  # it carries the freight leg
        + ((t.get("tooling_eur") or 0) - (std.get("tooling_eur") or 0)) / sold * cash_now
        - ppm / 1e6 * ((t.get("chargeback_eur_per_complaint") or 0) - (std.get("chargeback_eur_per_complaint") or 0))
        + supplier.get("extra", 0.0)
    )


def _soft(gap):
    """Margin points below the sustainable margin, as they cost: none above it, quadratic over
    the first 5 points, linear beyond - no kink."""
    if gap <= 0:
        return 0.0
    return gap * gap / 10 if gap <= 5 else gap - 2.5


def relationship_cost(case, terms, standard=None, supplier=None, value=None):
    """Strategic and bottleneck goals only: EUR for every margin point the deal leaves the supplier
    below `sustainable_margin_pct`, per year covered. `supplier["full_cost"]` (EUR per unit) is your
    estimate of its full cost; `value` overrides `supplier_value`. Without an estimate: 0."""
    b = case["buyer"]
    per_point, sustainable = b.get("relationship_eur_per_point"), b.get("sustainable_margin_pct")
    if b.get("category_goal") not in RELATIONSHIP_GOALS or not per_point or not sustainable or not supplier:
        return 0.0
    t = closing_terms(case, terms, standard)
    worth = value if value is not None else supplier_value(case, t, supplier)
    margin = (worth - supplier["full_cost"]) / worth * 100
    return per_point * _soft(sustainable - margin) * _years(case, t)


def cost_breakdown(case, terms, standard=None, supplier=None):
    """C by part. `standard`: the supplier's standard terms for anything the term sheet leaves out.
    `supplier`: your estimate of the supplier for the relationship term (`supplier_value`)."""
    b, t = case["buyer"], closing_terms(case, terms, standard)
    if t.get("unit_price") is None:
        raise ValueError("no unit_price: a term sheet without a price has no cost")
    years = _years(case, t)
    committed = t["volume_per_year"] * years  # bought, needed or not
    covered = min(t["volume_per_year"], b["need_per_year"]) * years
    pre = _units_before(case, t, years)
    at_new_price = (committed - pre) * t["unit_price"]
    spend = pre * (b.get("current_unit_price") or t["unit_price"]) + at_new_price
    per_defect = b.get("cost_per_defect", 0)
    defect_cost = per_defect - min(t.get("chargeback_eur_per_complaint") or 0, per_defect)
    index = index_risk = 0.0
    if clause := t.get("index_clause"):
        path = b.get("index_paths", {}).get(clause["series"], 0.0)
        moved = max(0.0, abs(path) - clause["deadband_pct"] / 100)
        index = at_new_price * clause["material_share"] * moved * math.copysign(1, path)
        index_risk = at_new_price * clause["material_share"] * b.get("index_risk_pct", 0) / 100
    uncovered = (b["need_per_year"] * b["horizon_years"] - covered) * b["fallback_unit_price"]
    need = b["need_lead_time_days"]
    return {
        "price": spend,
        "uncovered_need": uncovered,
        "fallback_risk": uncovered * b.get("fallback_risk_pct", 0) / 100,
        "payment_terms": spend * b["interest_rate"] * (b["reference_payment_days"] - t["payment_days"]) / 360,
        "freight": committed * b["freight_eur_per_unit"][t["incoterm"]],
        "late_delivery": b.get("late_cost_per_day", 0) * max(0, t["lead_time_days"] - need),
        "quality": committed * (t.get("ppm_commitment") or 0) / 1e6 * defect_cost,
        "tooling": t.get("tooling_eur") or 0.0,
        "index_clause": index,
        "index_risk": index_risk,
        "relationship": relationship_cost(case, t, supplier=supplier),
    }


def total_cost(case, terms, standard=None, supplier=None):
    """C in EUR; infinite for terms without a price (e.g. a supplier that quotes none), so such a
    sheet is never the cheapest and never beats an alternative."""
    if closing_terms(case, terms, standard).get("unit_price") is None:
        return math.inf
    return round(sum(cost_breakdown(case, terms, standard, supplier).values()), 2)


def score(c_open, c_deal, c_best):
    if c_deal is None:
        return 0.0
    if c_open - c_best <= 0.01:  # no room to negotiate: matching the best is full marks
        return 1.0 if c_deal <= c_best + 0.01 else 0.0
    return min(1.0, max(0.0, (c_open - c_deal) / (c_open - c_best)))


def must_haves_ok(case, terms, standard=None):
    t = closing_terms(case, terms, standard)
    for m in case["buyer"].get("must_haves", []):
        value = t.get(m["field"])
        if value is None and m["op"] not in ("==", "!="):
            return False
        if not OPS[m["op"]](value, m["value"]):
            return False
    return True


def snap(case, field, value):
    """The allowed value closest to `value` (case `term_options`), else `value` unchanged."""
    options = case.get("term_options", {}).get(field)
    if not options or value in options:
        return value
    if isinstance(value, int | float) and all(isinstance(o, int | float) for o in options):
        return min(options, key=lambda o: (abs(o - value), o))
    return options[0]


def complete_offer(case, terms):
    """A valid term sheet: exactly the negotiable fields, gaps from the buyer's plan, snapped."""
    plan = closing_terms(case, {"unit_price": None})
    freight = case["buyer"]["freight_eur_per_unit"]
    plan["incoterm"] = min(freight, key=freight.get)  # when asking, ask for the cheapest freight
    out = {}
    for field in case["negotiable"]:
        value = terms.get(field, plan.get(field))
        if value is None and case.get("term_options", {}).get(field):
            value = case["term_options"][field][0]
        value = snap(case, field, value)
        out[field] = round(value, 2) if field == "unit_price" and value is not None else value
    return out

"""Hard rules that keep a case from scoring 0 by mistake. Code, not judgement; checked before every
send and every accept, whatever the strategy decided.

Accept:  the sheet is the supplier's current standing offer; it keeps every must-have on the terms
         it would really close on (sheet, then the supplier's standard terms from its quote PDF) -
         and a must-have field we cannot read from either counts as broken; C is finite and beats
         the alternative - and, when there is one, the cheapest opening too (else the alternative
         scores at least as much).
Send:    every term sheet carries exactly the negotiable fields with allowed values and keeps the
         must-haves (a supplier may agree to any sheet we send, and we must be able to accept it);
         every cited ID exists in the data, the case's facts or this session's offers - a sentence
         whose IDs are all unknown goes, and so does a threat or an "other offer" without a rival's
         offer cited (conduct.py); at most 3 sheets and 20 refs.
"""

import math
import re

from arena_kit.cost import must_haves_ok

from negotiator.conduct import unsupported_sentences

ID_RE = re.compile(r"\b(?:idx|quote|offer|sc|qn|po|cost|fc|news|doc|ctr):[\w.:@#/-]*\w")
MAX_SHEETS = 3
MAX_REFS = 20


def unreadable_must_have_fields(case: dict, terms: dict, standard: dict | None) -> list[str]:
    """Must-have fields neither the sheet, the supplier's standard terms nor the case fixes.

    `closing_terms` fills such gaps from the buyer's plan (e.g. lead time = what we need), which
    would let a sheet pass that the arena closes on the supplier's real standard - unknown to us."""
    known = {**(standard or {}), **case.get("fixed_terms", {}), **{k: v for k, v in terms.items() if v is not None}}
    return [m["field"] for m in case["buyer"].get("must_haves", []) if m["field"] not in known]


def accept_problems(neg, supplier_id: str, term_sheet_id: str | None) -> list[str]:
    """Why accepting this sheet would be a mistake (empty: safe)."""
    t = neg.threads.get(supplier_id)
    if t is None:
        return ["unknown supplier"]
    standing_id, terms = t.standing
    problems = []
    if not term_sheet_id or term_sheet_id != standing_id:
        # the arena closes on the primary sheet whatever id we send (P10): only that one can be accepted
        problems.append(f"{term_sheet_id} is not the standing offer {standing_id}")
    if not terms or terms.get("unit_price") is None:
        problems.append("the standing offer has no price")
        return problems
    std = t.standard_terms
    if missing := unreadable_must_have_fields(neg.case, terms, std):
        problems.append(f"must-have field(s) {missing} unknown: no quote PDF standard terms")
    if not must_haves_ok(neg.case, terms, std):
        problems.append("breaks a must-have")
    c = neg.cost(supplier_id, terms)
    if not math.isfinite(c):
        problems.append("C is not finite")
    elif c >= neg.c_alt:
        problems.append(f"C {c:,.0f} does not beat the alternative {neg.c_alt:,.0f}")
    elif math.isfinite(neg.c_alt) and c >= neg.c_open:
        # a deal no better than the cheapest opening scores 0; the alternative scores at least that
        problems.append(f"C {c:,.0f} is not better than the opening {neg.c_open:,.0f}")
    return problems


def sheet_problems(case: dict, terms: dict) -> list[str]:
    problems = []
    negotiable = case["negotiable"]
    if set(terms) != set(negotiable):
        problems.append(f"fields {sorted(terms)} != negotiable {sorted(negotiable)}")
    options = case.get("term_options", {})
    for f, v in terms.items():
        if f == "unit_price":
            if not isinstance(v, int | float) or v <= 0:
                problems.append(f"unit_price {v!r}")
        elif options.get(f) and v not in options[f]:
            problems.append(f"{f}={v!r} not in options")
    if not must_haves_ok(case, terms):
        problems.append("breaks a must-have")
    return problems


def known_id(neg, ref: str) -> bool:
    if neg.data and neg.data.fact(ref):
        return True
    if ref in (neg.case.get("facts") or {}):
        return True
    return any(
        s.get("term_sheet_id") == ref
        for t in neg.threads.values()
        for m in t.supplier_messages
        for s in m.get("term_sheets") or []
    )


def clean_message(neg, supplier_id: str, message: dict) -> tuple[dict, list[str]]:
    """The message with invalid sheets and unknown IDs removed, and what was removed."""
    removed: list[str] = []
    sheets = []
    for sheet in (message.get("term_sheets") or [])[:MAX_SHEETS]:
        problems = sheet_problems(neg.case, sheet.get("terms", {}))
        if problems:
            removed.append(f"sheet {sheet.get('terms')}: {'; '.join(problems)}")
        elif sheet not in sheets:
            sheets.append(sheet)
    refs = []
    for ref in message.get("refs") or []:
        if known_id(neg, ref):
            if ref not in refs:
                refs.append(ref)
        else:
            removed.append(f"ref {ref}")

    def keep(m: re.Match) -> str:
        if known_id(neg, m.group(0)):
            return m.group(0)
        removed.append(f"body id {m.group(0)}")
        return ""

    # conduct.py: no claim without its source, no threat or "other offer" we cannot show
    rival_ids = {
        s.get("term_sheet_id")
        for other, t in neg.threads.items()
        if other != supplier_id
        for m in t.supplier_messages
        for s in m.get("term_sheets") or []
    }
    rival_cited = any(r in rival_ids or r.startswith("quote:") for r in refs)
    body, unsupported = unsupported_sentences(
        message.get("body") or "", ID_RE, lambda i: known_id(neg, i), rival_cited
    )
    removed += [f"unsupported sentence: {s}" for s in unsupported]
    body = ID_RE.sub(keep, body)
    body = re.sub(r"\s*\(\s*[,;\s]*\)", "", body)
    out = {**message, "body": body[:8000], "subject": (message.get("subject") or "")[:300], "refs": refs[:MAX_REFS]}
    if "term_sheets" in message:
        out["term_sheets"] = sheets
    return out, removed

"""Ground truth before the first move: where the supplier cannot go below, and what we accept at most.

  lower bound  the supplier's floor price: its full cost (should-cost of its own plant, moved with the
               part's cost drivers since the estimate, scaled by country), a little under it when it has
               sold below cost before; without a should-cost, the price history minus a wide margin.
  upper bound  the most we accept if the deal is at risk - never said, never offered: the price the
               market justifies (cost drivers x index moves) or what this supplier usually settles at
               (asked minus its typical give), whichever is lower; never below the lower bound, never
               above its quote.

Both are prices per the case's price unit; the strategy turns them into C with the cost function.
Pure SQL and arithmetic: milliseconds, so it runs after the session opened without touching the clock.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from negotiator.data import WorldData

# full cost relative to a German cost base (company.md, should-cost rule of thumb)
COUNTRY_FACTOR = {"DE": 1.0, "AT": 1.05, "CH": 1.05, "CZ": 0.82, "PL": 0.82, "HU": 0.82, "TR": 0.75, "CN": 0.7}
BELOW_COST_FLOOR = 0.95  # a supplier that sold below full cost may do so again, not by much
NO_COST_FLOOR = 0.90  # without a should-cost: 10 % under its quote
NO_COST_FLOOR_RELATIONSHIP = 0.95  # ... 5 % where squeezing a strategic supplier costs us
# The floor as a share of the opening quote, backed out of the practice cases' C_best (the price that
# reaches C_best on the best structure; 12 suppliers, 10 cases, 2026-10-10). Should-cost missed it by 16 %
# on average, "quote x 0.90" by 11 %, this table by about 4 %. Where a case's kind is unseen, the goal.
# Where a supplier ends, as a share of its quote - two levels, kept simple on purpose. When only the price of a
# running relationship is at stake (a price increase, a renewal) it barely moves; when competition, material or
# capacity give us a lever it moves about 14 %. Leave-one-out over the practice cases' C_best: 3.4 % mean error,
# better than seven per-type factors (4.1 %) and robust to case types practice never shows. The live belief
# (belief.py) corrects the rest from the supplier's own replies.
PRICE_ONLY_TYPES = {"price_increase", "renewal"}
FLOOR_PRICE_ONLY = 0.99
FLOOR_WITH_LEVERS = 0.86
UPPER_MARGIN = 0.05  # we accept at most 5 % above the calibrated floor when the deal is at risk
DEFAULT_GIVE_PCT = 2.5  # renewals settled 2.5 points under the ask on average (negotiation_history)


@dataclass
class Driver:
    series: str
    weight: float
    change_pct: float
    refs: list[str]


@dataclass
class GroundTruth:
    supplier_id: str
    part_id: str | None
    current_price: float | None
    open_price: float | None
    full_cost: float | None = None
    full_cost_source: str = ""
    lower: float | None = None
    upper: float | None = None
    asked_pct: float | None = None
    justified_pct: float | None = None  # what the cost drivers support over the last 12 months
    give_pct: float = DEFAULT_GIVE_PCT
    drivers: list[Driver] = field(default_factory=list)
    grounded: bool = False  # the floor rests on a cost estimate (should-cost, breakdown), not a guess
    notes: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)

    @property
    def market_supports_ask(self) -> bool:
        """The indices back the supplier: arguing them would hurt us."""
        return (
            self.asked_pct is not None and self.justified_pct is not None and self.justified_pct >= self.asked_pct - 0.5
        )

    def summary(self) -> dict:
        return {
            "part": self.part_id,
            "current": self.current_price,
            "open": self.open_price,
            "full_cost": self.full_cost,
            "full_cost_source": self.full_cost_source,
            "lower": self.lower,
            "upper": self.upper,
            "asked_pct": self.asked_pct,
            "justified_pct": self.justified_pct,
            "give_pct": self.give_pct,
            "market_supports_ask": self.market_supports_ask,
            "grounded": self.grounded,
            "notes": self.notes,
        }


def justified_change(data: WorldData, part_id: str, months: int = 12) -> tuple[float | None, list[Driver]]:
    """Sum over the part's cost drivers of weight x index change over the last `months` (the share
    no driver covers is taken as flat). The IDs make each driver a checkable argument."""
    drivers = []
    total, found = 0.0, False
    for d in data.query("SELECT series_id, weight FROM cost_drivers WHERE part_id = ?", (part_id,)):
        change = data.index_change(d["series_id"], months)
        if not change or not d["weight"]:
            continue
        earlier, later, pct = change
        drivers.append(Driver(d["series_id"], d["weight"], round(pct, 2), [earlier, later]))
        total += d["weight"] * pct
        found = True
    return (round(total, 2) if found else None), drivers


def _cost_drift(data: WorldData, part_id: str, since_month: str) -> float:
    """How the part's cost moved since the should-cost estimate, by its cost drivers (fraction)."""
    total = 0.0
    for d in data.query("SELECT series_id, weight FROM cost_drivers WHERE part_id = ?", (part_id,)):
        rows = data.query(
            "SELECT month, value FROM index_values WHERE series_id = ? AND month >= ? ORDER BY month",
            (d["series_id"], since_month),
        )
        if len(rows) >= 2 and rows[0]["value"]:
            total += (d["weight"] or 0) * (rows[-1]["value"] / rows[0]["value"] - 1)
    return total


def full_cost(data: WorldData, part_id: str, supplier_id: str) -> tuple[float | None, str]:
    """The supplier's full cost per unit now: its own plant's should-cost, else the German estimate
    scaled by its country; moved with the cost drivers since the estimate."""
    rows = data.query(
        "SELECT unit_cost, supplier_id, estimate_date FROM should_cost WHERE part_id = ? ORDER BY estimate_date DESC",
        (part_id,),
    )
    if not rows:
        return None, ""
    own = [r for r in rows if r["supplier_id"] == supplier_id]
    if own:
        row, factor, source = own[0], 1.0, "own plant"
    else:
        generic = [r for r in rows if not r["supplier_id"]]
        if not generic:
            return None, ""  # another supplier's plant says little about this one
        country = (data.supplier(supplier_id).get("country") or "DE").upper()
        row, factor, source = generic[0], COUNTRY_FACTOR.get(country, 1.0), f"DE base x {country}"
    drift = _cost_drift(data, part_id, (row["estimate_date"] or "")[:7]) if row["estimate_date"] else 0.0
    return round(row["unit_cost"] * factor * (1 + drift), 2), source


def last_price(data: WorldData, part_id: str, supplier_id: str) -> float | None:
    rows = data.query(
        "SELECT price FROM price_conditions WHERE part_id = ? AND supplier_id = ? ORDER BY valid_from DESC LIMIT 1",
        (part_id, supplier_id),
    )
    return rows[0]["price"] if rows else None


def estimate(data: WorldData | None, case: dict, supplier_id: str, open_price: float | None, traits=()) -> GroundTruth:
    parts = case.get("parts") or []
    part = parts[0] if len(parts) == 1 else None  # a kit's price is not one part's cost
    buyer = case.get("buyer", {})
    current = buyer.get("current_unit_price")
    gt = GroundTruth(supplier_id, part, current, open_price)
    if open_price is None:
        gt.notes.append("no quoted price")
        return gt
    if data and part:
        current = current or last_price(data, part, supplier_id)
        gt.current_price = current
        gt.full_cost, gt.full_cost_source = full_cost(data, part, supplier_id)
        gt.justified_pct, gt.drivers = justified_change(data, part)
    if data:
        gives = data.query(
            "SELECT asked_pct - settled_pct AS give FROM negotiation_history WHERE supplier_id = ? "
            "AND asked_pct IS NOT NULL AND settled_pct IS NOT NULL",
            (supplier_id,),
        )
        if gives:
            gt.give_pct = round(sum(g["give"] for g in gives) / len(gives), 2)
    trigger = (data.fact(case["trigger_doc"]) if data and case.get("trigger_doc") else None) or {}
    if trigger.get("supplier") == supplier_id and trigger.get("asked_pct") is not None:
        gt.asked_pct = trigger["asked_pct"]
    elif current and open_price > current:
        gt.asked_pct = round((open_price / current - 1) * 100, 2)

    # lower bound: where the supplier ends - price-only talks vs talks with a lever (see FLOOR_PRICE_ONLY)
    if gt.full_cost:
        gt.notes.append(f"full cost {gt.full_cost} ({gt.full_cost_source})")
        gt.grounded = True  # a cost estimate exists: an argument and the margin term, not the floor
    factor = floor_factor(case)
    gt.lower = round(open_price * factor, 2)
    gt.notes.append(f"floor = quote x {factor} ({case.get('type')}, {case.get('buyer', {}).get('category_goal')})")

    # upper bound: the most we accept when the deal is at risk - a little above where suppliers of this kind end
    gt.upper = round(min(open_price, gt.lower * (1 + UPPER_MARGIN)), 2)
    return gt


def floor_factor(case: dict) -> float:
    """The supplier's floor as a share of its quote: price-only talks vs talks with a lever."""
    single = len(case.get("suppliers") or []) <= 1
    return FLOOR_PRICE_ONLY if single and case.get("type") in PRICE_ONLY_TYPES else FLOOR_WITH_LEVERS

def _full_cost(case: dict, p: Profile, terms: dict, charge: float) -> float:
    """The supplier's full cost per unit that makes the kit's relationship term equal the recorded charge."""
    lo, hi = 0.0, terms["unit_price"] * 1.5
    for _ in range(50):

    return hi


def estimate(p: Profile, full_cost: float | None = None) -> dict | None:
    """The kit's `supplier` argument for the relationship term of C, where the full cost is known."""
    cost = p.full_cost if full_cost is None else full_cost
    if cost is None:
        return None
    return {"standard": p.ref, "interest_rate": max(0.0, p.rates.get("pay", 0.08)), "full_cost": cost}


def load_model(path: Path) -> dict:
    return as_objects(json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")))


def as_objects(model: dict) -> dict:
    """A model as the simulator uses it: profiles as objects (also for a freshly calibrated one)."""
    raw = json.loads(json.dumps(model))
    raw["profiles"] = {k: Profile(**v) for k, v in raw["profiles"].items()}

import json,glob,math
from arena_kit.cost import RELATIONSHIP_GOALS
seen={}
for f in sorted(glob.glob('runs/*/sessions/*.json')):
    d=json.load(open(f)); o=d['outcome']; case=d['case']; b=case['buyer']
    if b.get('category_goal') not in RELATIONSHIP_GOALS or not o.get('deal'): continue
    ch=(o.get('cost_breakdown') or {}).get('relationship') or 0
    t=o['terms']; yrs=min(t['contract_months']/12, b['horizon_years'])
    cid=o['case_id']
    if cid not in seen:
        seen[cid]=set()
        op=d['state'].get('opening')
        print('\n',cid,case.get('type'),'goal',b['category_goal'],'sm',b['sustainable_margin_pct'],'pt',b['relationship_eur_per_point'],'cur',b.get('current_unit_price'),'rate',b['interest_rate'],'refpay',b['reference_payment_days'],'hor',b['horizon_years'],'fallback',b['fallback_unit_price'])
        print('  opening',json.dumps(op)[:700])
        print('  freight',b['freight_eur_per_unit'],'fixed',case.get('fixed_terms'))
    if ch<=0: continue
    x=ch/b['relationship_eur_per_point']/yrs
    gap=math.sqrt(10*x) if x<=2.5 else x+2.5
    m=b['sustainable_margin_pct']-gap
    key=(t['unit_price'],t['payment_days'],t.get('incoterm'),t.get('contract_months'),t.get('volume_per_year'),t.get('chargeback_eur_per_complaint'),t.get('ppm_commitment'),t.get('effective_date'),t.get('tooling_eur'))
    if key in seen[cid]: continue
    seen[cid].add(key)
    print('  ',key,'charge',ch,'margin%',round(m,3),'fc/worth',round(1-m/100,5),'fc per price',round(t['unit_price']*(1-m/100),3))
E

The horizon starts at the fixed or earliest `effective_date` option; `index_path` is the case's
expected move of the clause's series.

**The supplier's margin** is `(value − full_cost) / value × 100`: `full_cost` is the supplier's
full cost per unit, `value` what the deal is worth to it in cash per unit - the price at its own
standard terms that would pay it the same: the price (units sold before the new price applies at
the current price), payment timing and tooling paid up front at what money is worth to **it** now
(more to a supplier short of cash), the freight leg it carries, chargebacks at the defect rate it
really has, and what a faster delivery, a larger volume or a tighter defect commitment costs or
brings it. A longer contract or an index clause is security for it, not cash, and does not count.
So a cash-short supplier that trades a lower price for faster payment is not squeezed.

## Should-cost
`should_cost.csv` estimates full cost without margin. For the parts of strategic and bottleneck
negotiations the category team modelled the current supplier's own plant (`supplier_id`, error about
5 %); the other rows use a German cost base with an error of 5-15 %. Rule of thumb for other countries'
full cost relative to Germany: AT and CH about 1.0-1.1, CZ, PL and HU about 0.8-0.85, TR about 0.75,
CN about 0.7.

## Category strategies
The LLM agent is a starting point, not a winner: it sees only what the case file points to.
Finding the data that moves a supplier is your job - the worked example below shows one way for
one kind of argument. Ideas beyond it: mine the notes and e-mails, read the suppliers' signals and
documents, send two or three term sheets to learn what a supplier values, ask its roles the right
questions, keep RFQ threads alive in parallel, and never leak urgency, a budget or a missing
alternative.

**Strategic and bottleneck cases** (`category_goal` `stabilise` or `secure_supply`) charge C for a
deal that leaves the supplier below a sustainable margin. Pass your estimate of the supplier to
price it - without one, `total_cost` leaves the term out:

```python
supplier = {"full_cost": 128.0, "interest_rate": 0.12, "standard": std}  # your estimate
total_cost(case, terms, std, supplier)
```

Repo: /home/vector/Desktop/Programming/EHLFinal2026 (read CLAUDE.md at the root first; Python 3.12, uv; package in `agent/`, run things with `cd agent && uv run ...`). We build a buyer agent for a negotiation arena. The final runs on 15-50 NEW hidden case briefs, so we want a free, offline check that the agent *understands a case brief correctly* before any negotiation - not a strategy tuner.

Goal: build an offline harness that feeds augmented case briefs to the step where our `tactical` strategy digests a case (no negotiation, no arena calls, no practice quota - NEVER call `negotiator play`/`run --set practice` or POST sessions), and compares what the agent derives with independently computed correct answers.

Background you need:
- Case JSON shape: see any recorded session `agent/runs/*/sessions/*.json` (key `case`, plus `state.opening` with each supplier's opening offer and `threads[sid].standard_terms`). There are 10 practice cases (case:P01,P02,P03,P04,P05,P07,P08,P10,P11,P18) and two demos (D01, D02) recorded there; kit simulator cases are in `negotiation-arena-kit/starter-kit/arena_kit/sim_cases/`. The submodule `negotiation-arena-kit/` is read-only. API field docs: `negotiation-arena-kit/brief/api.md`; cost function: `negotiation-arena-kit/starter-kit/arena_kit/cost.py`.
- The digest step is `Tactical.prepare` in `agent/src/negotiator/strategy/tactical.py` (emits a `plan` event: goal, policy, open_c, target_c, lower_c, upper_c, ground truth) on a `Negotiation` from `agent/src/negotiator/session.py`. Look at `agent/tests/` and `agent/src/negotiator/sim/` (the local simulator already builds Negotiation objects offline from recorded sessions) to find the cheapest way to construct a Negotiation from a case dict + opening offers without network.
- Recorded outcomes contain the arena's own `c_open`, and `cost_breakdown`, so for the unmodified practice cases you can validate that our `neg.c_open` equals the arena's c_open.

What to build (new files only - another agent is editing `tactical.py`, `session.py`, `guards.py` right now; do NOT edit existing source files, do NOT commit, do NOT touch git branches):
1. A generator producing 30-50 variants from the 12 recorded cases: scaled prices, volumes, horizons (1/2/3 years), different interest rates/reference payment days, different freight tables and incoterm options, changed fixed vs negotiable field sets, must-haves added/removed, alternatives present/absent, category_goal swapped (leverage/routine/stabilise/secure_supply/quality_first), relationship parameters present/absent, index clause options and index_paths, missing optional fields, opening offers missing fields (e.g. no payment_days), multi-supplier and single-supplier, and several cases with an UNKNOWN `type` and/or unknown `category_goal` string, unknown extra negotiable fields, and empty `parts`. Deterministic (seeded). Do not copy data-package values into source code: derive variants at runtime from the recorded session files (if the runs directory is absent, the test should skip).
2. For each variant compute the expected answers independently with `arena_kit.cost` directly (not through our session code): C of the opening (c_open = cheapest opening that keeps must-haves), c_alt, whether the goal is a relationship goal, must-have verdict of the opening, and that a sent sheet built by the strategy's first move is valid (exactly the negotiable fields, allowed option values, must-haves kept - see `guards.sheet_problems`).
3. Run only prepare (and, if cheap and offline, the first buyer message construction) and compare: no exception; c_open/c_alt match; plan numbers finite and ordered sensibly (target_c <= upper_c <= open_c, upper_c <= c_alt when an alternative exists); first ask price is positive and below/equal the opening price; for relationship goals the ask is not below what the code's own floor says; unknown type/goal does not crash and falls back to a sane default.
4. Put it at `agent/tests/test_brief_variants.py` (pytest, must pass or xfail-with-reason for genuine agent bugs you find - do not hide a bug by loosening the check) plus, if useful, a helper module under `agent/tests/`. Run `cd agent && uv run pytest tests/test_brief_variants.py -q` and `uv run ruff check tests/` until clean.

Report back (concise): the files you added, how many variants, and - most important - a list of every real misunderstanding/crash you found in the agent, each with the variant that triggers it, the file:line responsible, expected vs actual. Clearly separate "verified bug" from "suspicion". No predictions or invented numbers.

input.prompt:
Repo: /home/vector/Desktop/Programming/EHLFinal2026 (read CLAUDE.md at the root and `agent/docs/backlog.md` first). We build a buyer agent for a negotiation arena; score per case = (C_open - C_deal)/(C_open - C_best), C from `negotiation-arena-kit/starter-kit/arena_kit/cost.py` (formula also in `negotiation-arena-kit/brief/api.md`). This is a READ-ONLY research task: do not edit files, do not run anything that calls the arena (`negotiator play/run`, POST), do not commit.

Data: every session we played is recorded in `agent/runs/<run>/sessions/<id>.json` (keys: `case` = the brief, `state.opening` = suppliers' opening offers with claims/signals/text, `threads[sid].messages` = full e-mail exchange incl. the supplier's structured `reasons`, `status`, term sheets, `outcome` with score, c_open, c_best, c_deal, cost_breakdown) and human-readable `<id>.md`. The data package is `negotiation-arena-kit/data/` (world.sqlite, facts.json, contracts, correspondence). `agent/docs/rejections.md` and `agent/docs/practice-analysis.md` summarise earlier reading.

Questions - answer each from the recorded evidence, quoting the supplier's own `reasons`/sentences with run/session ids:

A. Raw-material cases P08 and P18 (type raw material surcharge, goal leverage). One team reached 0.91 on P08 (house agent 0.75, our best 0.626); on P18 the best is 0.68 (ours 0.618). Find the big lever we miss. For each case: list the negotiable fields, term_options (especially `index_clause` options, `effective_date`, `contract_months`, `payment_days`, volume), `index_paths`, `index_risk_pct`, fixed terms, the alternative, must-haves. Then, using `arena_kit.cost.total_cost` offline on the recorded case dict (run python via `cd agent && uv run python ...`), enumerate the grid of all non-price term combinations and for each find the unit price at which C equals the recorded `c_best`; report which structure makes C_best reachable at the highest (most plausible) price - i.e. what package C_best probably is. Check specifically: (1) does an index clause with a falling index path lower C substantially (index term = spend x material_share x move)? what are the index paths' signs? (2) is the surcharge separable from the base price in any field or in the supplier's text/attachments (cost breakdown xlsx)? (3) is metal double-counted (base price already contains it)? (4) effective-date effects (units before the date at the current price). Also list every lever the supplier itself named in its replies on these two cases and whether we ever gave it, and every argument of ours it rejected/accepted with its stated reason.

B. P11 (quality, goal quality_first; best 0.81, house 0.31, ours 0.692; 17 of 20 teams beat the house): same grid analysis - which term combination yields C_best, what ppm/chargeback/payment terms weigh in C, what the supplier asked for (faster payment, dropping chargebacks) and what a sheet granting those costs us in C versus the price it could buy.

C. Stabilise cases P02, P03, P01, secure_supply P10: from the supplier `reasons`, does the supplier ever refuse a price as below its cost, or signal its floor/cost/standard payment terms? Quote. For P10: the supplier's first reply was a final offer with an alternative - what reasons did it give and is there any lever (volume commitment, contract length, lead time) that sessions show moved it?

D. Bluffing rules: we consider letting the buyer say "we have alternatives" without naming one / act indifferent / never reveal its limit. From `negotiation-arena-kit/brief/*.md` (brief, api, any rules/FAQ), `agent/docs/knowledge/competitions-info.md` and the recorded supplier reasons: how does the supplier bot treat unsupported claims (are claims verified? is there a penalty/`contradicted` status? did any of our sessions get a reason like "you cited no data" or reacted to pressure/ultimatums)? Quote the rule text and any session evidence. Also quote any rule about prompt injection / manipulating the supplier bot.

E. Opening anchor evidence: across all recorded practice sessions, per case, tabulate our first asked unit price as % below the supplier's opening price versus the supplier's first counter-move and the final score, to see whether deeper first asks went with better outcomes or with walk-aways/final offers. Note the user's idea: ask for less than we are ready to accept at the start (aggressive anchor).

Deliver a compact report: for each of A-E the findings, the concrete actionable lever (what the agent should send differently), and the evidence (session ids, quotes, computed C numbers with the terms used). Only measured/computed numbers; mark anything you infer as an inference.

    def _optimise(self, neg: Negotiation, sid: str, terms: dict) -> dict:
        """Coordinate descent over the non-price options: each field set to what minimises C.

        On a tie in C the supplier's own value wins: a term that costs us nothing is given away for free (e.g. a
        looser ppm when the chargeback already covers our defect cost)."""
        options = neg.case.get("term_options", {})
        best = dict(terms)
        given = dict(terms)
        for _ in range(2):
            for f in neg.case["negotiable"]:
                if f == "unit_price" or not options.get(f):
                    continue

                def key(value, f=f):
                    trial = {**best, f: value}
                    ok = neg.keeps_must_haves(sid, trial)
                    cost = round(neg.cost(sid, trial), 2) if ok else math.inf
                    return (cost, value != given.get(f), repr(value))

# The supplier simulator (`negotiator sim`)

As of 10 October 2026, fitted from 84 recorded arena sessions (54 sandbox, 30 practice).

A local arena between `arena-sim` (the kit's fixed script) and the real bots: the kit's API, the 12 cases we have
played, the arena's own `C_open` and `C_best` per case as the yardstick, and suppliers fitted from our replays. It
costs no practice session and no token; 4 strategies x 12 cases x 5 repeats take about 30 seconds.

```sh
cd agent
uv run negotiator sim calibrate                        # fit from runs/ -> data/sim/model.json (git-ignored)
uv run negotiator sim check                            # how well the fit predicts sessions it has not seen
uv run negotiator sim bench baseline tactical --reps 5 # strategies on the simulator, next to their arena scores
uv run negotiator sim bench tactical --strangers       # each supplier with the habits of another one
uv run negotiator sim bench old new --opponents all --jitter --reps 3   # the opponent pool, floors moved
uv run negotiator sim serve --port 8100                # as a local arena for `negotiator --url ...`
```

**The usual commands, on the simulator.** `sim serve` is the arena's API on `http://127.0.0.1:8100`; add `--sim` to
any command and it talks to it instead of the arena - same client, runner, strategies, reports and chats:

```sh
uv run negotiator sim serve                                   # terminal 1
uv run negotiator --sim run --set practice --strategy tactical   # terminal 2: all 12 cases (--cases to pick)
uv run negotiator --sim play case:P05 --strategy llm
```

`http://127.0.0.1:8100/leaderboard` is its board and `/replay/<session id>` a finished case as a page. `sim bench`
is only a loop over the same thing: it starts this server per repeat and plays through the same runner.

Simulator runs go to `agent/runs-sim/`, apart from `runs/`: they are not benchmark records and never enter
`negotiator stats`.

## What is fitted, and from what

| Part | Source in the replays |
|---|---|
| Opening and standard terms | each supplier's quote e-mail and quote PDF |
| What a term is worth to it (payment days, lead time, effective date, contract length, index clause, ppm) | the alternatives it quotes in one e-mail ("alternatively, with 14 days net: EUR ...") - two prices for one position |
| Its floor | the price at which the best package it could accept costs exactly the `C_best` the arena published |
| How far it moves per e-mail | its recorded steps as a share of the gap to the floor, by what the buyer did: moved, stood still, a rival quote, another argument that convinced it, the second half of an approved step |
| When it calls an offer final | the reply number of its recorded final offers |

`C_open` computed by the simulator equals the arena's on all 12 cases, and the fitted floor reproduces `C_best` on 9
of them. On the other three (P01, P02, P04) the floor is a guess below the lowest offer seen; in every case no
simulated offer can be cheaper than `C_best`.

## How far to trust it

Measured, not assumed. `negotiator sim check` leaves one session out, fits on the rest, replays that session's buyer
e-mails and scores the offer standing when the buyer accepted.

| Played end to end, simulator mean against arena mean (8 strategy-case pairs, sandbox) | 0.037 |

# Git rules

## Commit messages: Conventional Commits

```
<type>(<scope>): <subject>

<body: why, not what — optional>

<footer: BREAKING CHANGE: ..., Refs: #123 — optional>
```

**Types**

| Type | Use for |
|---|---|
| `feat` | New user-facing behaviour |
| `fix` | Bug fix |
| `refactor` | Code change with no behaviour change |
| `perf` | Performance improvement |
| `test` | Adding or fixing tests only |
| `docs` | Documentation only (README, AGENTS.md, .agents/, comments) |
| `style` | Formatting only (ruff format, prettier); no logic |
| `build` | Dependencies, lockfiles, Makefile, the submodule pin |
| `ci` | CI pipelines |
| `chore` | Repo maintenance that fits nothing above (gitignore, tooling config) |
| `revert` | Reverting an earlier commit |

**Scopes** (optional, one per commit): `agent` (the negotiator package), `strategy` (negotiation logic in
`agent/src/negotiator/strategy/`), `kit` (the submodule pin), `repo` (root files). Omit the scope when a
change spans several areas.

**Subject**
- Imperative mood, lower case, no trailing period: `add item search endpoint`, not `Added item search.`
- At most 72 characters for the whole first line.
- Describe the effect, not the file: `fix(agent): retry a dropped reply with the same move id`.

**Body**: wrap at 72 characters; explain the reason and any trade-off. Required for `BREAKING CHANGE`
(also mark the type with `!`: `feat(agent)!: rename the run command to play-set`).

# Agent strategies: logic and results

As of 10 October 2026, commit `8670be2`.

**Case score:** a number from 0 to 1, `(C_open − C_deal) / (C_open − C_best)`. It is the share of the possible saving
we got, measured from the best opening offer.

**Where we played:** every run was on the arena's sandbox, cases D01 and D02, against real supplier bots. No practice
quota (200 sessions per day) was spent.

**The simulator is e2e testing, not a metric:**
- Runs on the local `arena-sim` check only the mechanics: client, runner, message format, closing a case.
- The result there is pass/fail. Its scripted supplier concedes a fixed 2 % per round, so its score is not used to
  compare strategies.
- Every strategy passes e2e: 3 of 3 deals, arguments `verified`.

## Strategies

| Strategy | Code | Author | LLM | Logic |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **baseline v1** (replaced) | `strategy/baseline.py` before `8670be2` | Mikhail Fadin | no | Target = opening price minus an anchor (leverage −10 %, routine −7 %, stabilise −4 %, secure_supply −3 %). Concessions on a fixed schedule: 0 → 30 → 50 → 65 → 78 → 88 → 95 % of the gap. Three term sheets: C
| **baseline v2** (current) | `strategy/baseline.py` (`8670be2`) | Mikhail Fadin | no | Everything from v1 plus three fixes from the sandbox analysis. **(1) Equal-C menu:** every sheet in a message costs us the same; the sheet on the supplier's own structure is cheaper by exactly how much worse that
| **llm** | `strategy/llm_strategy.py` | Mikhail Fadin | yes (currently `ollama:qwen3.6`) | Runs on top of baseline v2. Before the session opens, the model reads the supplier's dossier (letters, notes, news, history, credit index) and builds a profile. Each round it picks the stance, concession shar
| **tactical** (default) | `strategy/tactical.py`, `profile.py`, `guards.py`, `lessons.py` | DavidtheRavinger | no | **Policy per category goal:** anchor, concession speed, reciprocity. About 12 supplier traits found in the data by regular expressions adjust it: cash-short, approval ladder, idle cap
| **judged / jev** (planned) | – | – | yes | Tactical at three aggressiveness levels (soft, normal, hard); a judge model picks the move. Waiting for the model. |

## Results: arena sandbox (real bots)

| Strategy | D01: price increase, stabilise | D02: RFQ, 2 suppliers, leverage | Mean | Rounds D01 / D02 | Time D01 / D02 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| baseline v1 | 0.268 | 0.425 | 0.346 | 5 / 9 | 91 / 187 s |
| llm (before fixes) | 0.100 | 0.455 | 0.277 | 4 / 7 | 130 / 167 s |
| llm (after fixes, before the equal-C menu) | 0.210 | 0.448 | 0.329 | 6 / 11 | 173 / 274 s |
| **baseline v2** | **0.843** | **0.629** | **0.736** | 3 / 8 | 76 / 162 s |
| llm on v2 | 0.663 | 0.545 | 0.604 | 3 / 8 | 90 / 175 s |
| tactical | 0.773 | 0.505 | 0.639 | 4 / 7 | – |

## Conclusions

1. **The mechanics drove the gain, not the LLM.** The equal-C menu and reciprocal concessions lifted baseline on the
   arena from 0.346 to 0.736. Tactical is built on the same ideas and is also far above the old baseline.
2. **The results are noisy.** One run per case, and the bots answer non-deterministically, so the gap between
   baseline v2 (0.736) and tactical (0.639) is not reliable. It needs repeated runs.
3. **Tactical probably trails on D02 because of its shallow anchor.** Its anchor is at most −15 % below the quote,
   while the supplier's floor there is about −24 % below the opening.
4. **The LLM layer does not pay off yet.** On v2 it is worse than plain baseline: the model concedes more cautiously
   than these bots require. The natural place for a model is choosing the aggressiveness (jev), not replacing the logic.
5. **The test base is narrow.** Everything was measured on two demo cases. The real practice cases with supplier data
   (P01–P19) are untested.

## What we learned about the supplier bots (trace and back office)

- **Term structure can matter more than price.** In D01 the best deal is a 24-month contract, 60 days' payment and a
  price valid from April, at about €50.13 per unit. With a 12-month contract the second year of the horizon is bought at
  the fallback price: roughly €30k more at almost the same unit price.
- **A supplier's floor can be far below its opening.** In D02 the best deal is about €13.0 per unit against openings of
  16.0 and 17.1 (−19 to −24 %). An early `agreed` to our offer means we overpaid.
- **The bots name their levers.** Examples: "Faster payment is welcome; we can reflect it in the price", "A binding
  higher volume would help".
- **Citing a cheaper rival works.** Example: "I give half the step now and check the rest".

"""Single-tactic experiments on top of the baseline: each variant changes one thing, so a benchmark run
shows what that tactic alone is worth against the supplier bots (results: docs/benchmarks/).
  lowball    a deeper opening anchor: ask for less than we need, so the middle lands in our favour
  questions  three questions in every e-mail: make answering us more work than agreeing
  polite     a warm, appreciative tone
  shelby     a curt, hard tone with a threat to place the order elsewhere
  budget     a ceiling set by a third party ("management released at most EUR X") that we do not cross
  trade      no price move without a move from the supplier, and said so: every option is a trade
Everything else - term sheets from C, arguments, holding and closing - is the baseline's.
"""
from dataclasses import dataclass
from negotiator.session import Negotiation
from negotiator.strategy.baseline import GOAL_ANCHOR, BaselineStrategy, SupplierPlan
from negotiator.telemetry import log
# tone -> (first e-mail, later e-mails, closing line or None)
TONES = {
    "polite": (
        "thank you very much for your quote and for the good cooperation - we appreciate the work your team puts "
        "into it. We would like to find a solution that works for both sides; as it stands the quote is above what "
        "we can accept.",
        "thank you for your reply and for moving towards us - we appreciate it. We have moved as well and hope you "
        "can take a further step.",
        "Thank you for your support - we are confident we will find an agreement.",
    ),
    "shelby": (
        "we have read your quote. It is not a number we will sign.",
        "you have moved a little. It is not enough. We have moved too, and we do not move twice for nothing.",
        "This order will be placed either way - with you or without you. Your move.",
    ),
}
QUESTIONS = [
    "What lead time can you commit to for the first call-off?",
    "Which share of your price is material, and which index does it follow?",
    "How much free capacity do you have for this part in the coming quarter?",
    "Who on your side has to approve a price below your quote?",
    "Would faster payment or a longer commitment help you more?",
    "What defect rate do you achieve on comparable parts?",
    "What would a higher annual volume change in your calculation?",
    "Which Incoterm and packaging are cheapest for you?",
    "Can you hold the price for the whole term without an index clause?",
]
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Tactic:
    name: str
    anchor_scale: float = 1.0  # multiplies the baseline's anchor per category goal
    tone: str | None = None  # a key of TONES; None: the baseline's wording
    questions_per_round: int = 0
    budget_share: float | None = None  # ceiling = target + share x (opening - target); None: no ceiling
    conditional: bool = False  # the supplier does not move -> we do not move at all
TACTICS = {
    t.name: t
    for t in (
        Tactic("lowball", anchor_scale=1.5),
        Tactic("questions", questions_per_round=3),
        Tactic("polite", tone="polite"),
        Tactic("shelby", tone="shelby"),
        Tactic("budget", budget_share=0.5),
        Tactic("trade", conditional=True),
    )
}
class ExperimentStrategy(BaselineStrategy):
    def __init__(self, tactic: Tactic, data=None, llm=None) -> None:
        super().__init__(data, llm)
        self.tactic = tactic
        self.name = tactic.name
        self.ceilings: dict[str, float] = {}
    def prepare(self, neg: Negotiation) -> None:
        super().prepare(neg)
        tac = self.tactic
        goal = neg.buyer.get("category_goal", "leverage")
        current = neg.buyer.get("current_unit_price")
        for sid, plan in self.plans.items():
            if plan.open_price is None or plan.target_price is None:
                continue
            if tac.anchor_scale != 1.0:
                base = min(plan.open_price, current) if current else plan.open_price
                target = base * (1 - GOAL_ANCHOR.get(goal, 0.06) * tac.anchor_scale)
                plan.target_price = round(min(max(target, plan.floor_price or 0.0), plan.open_price), 2)
            if tac.budget_share is not None:
                gap = plan.open_price - plan.target_price
                self.ceilings[sid] = round(plan.target_price + tac.budget_share * gap, 2)
            neg.recorder.event(
                "experiment",
                session_id=neg.session_id,
                case_id=neg.case_id,
                supplier_id=sid,
                tactic=tac.name,
                target_price=plan.target_price,
                ceiling=self.ceilings.get(sid),

1. Writer. Tactical decides everything: price, terms, the term sheets, which concession, which cited IDs, hold/accept. The LLM only writes the e-mail body around that decision: a reason, one question about the supplier's constraints, a partner-like tone in `stabilise`/`secure_supply` cases, firm and factual in `leverage`. Lessons already measured that the prompt must respect (see TRYED.md, `agent/docs/rejections.md`, `agent/docs/knowledge/`): no budget ceiling, no threats or "we have other offers" without a cited rival offer ID, no ultimatum tone, never reveal our limit/target/upper bound or urgency or a missing alternative, do not repeat an argument already used, one fresh citable argument per round, answer what the supplier asked (e.g. "which volume can you commit to?" -> the sheet's volume is binding), no prompt-injection attempts at the supplier.
2. Validator on every outgoing message, in code: every number in the text must match what tactical chose (prices, days, months, volumes, percentages from the cited facts) - no other prices; every ID in the text is one tactical chose to cite; no mention of our limit; no acceptance or commitment language beyond the sheets; it passes the existing send guard (`guards.clean_message`, `conduct.py`) unchanged. If the check fails -> send tactical's template text.
3. Timeout and fallback: an LLM error or a call slower than a few seconds (make it a setting; the final has 8-minute waves and many cases in parallel) -> the template. Count fallbacks in telemetry.
4. Low temperature.
5. Reader (second priority; do the writer first): turns the supplier's reply into structured hints (stated reasons, constraints such as capacity/cash/margin, levers it names, whether it signals a last word). It is a hint, not a command: tactical already reads replies with regular expressions (`menu.REQUESTS`, `reply_signals`); the reader may only ADD requested levers / signals where the regexes miss them, and is ignored when parsing fails or contradicts the term sheets.

Verify, free only
- Unit tests for the validator (a text with a wrong price, an unknown ID, a leaked limit, a threat -> fallback) and for timeout/error fallback, with a fake LLM client.
- `negotiator sim bench` as a smoke test that nothing breaks.
- Sandbox: plain `tactical` versus your strategy on D01 and D02, at least three repetitions of the LLM strategy (LLM text varies), using the cheapest sensible model first (look at how earlier runs passed `--llm claude-code:haiku` / `claude-code:opus`; if no provider works in this environment, say so and stop at the offline tests). Record the runs as the repo requires: a benchmark record under `agent/docs/benchmarks/`, a line in its README, rows in `agent/docs/runs.md` (sandbox table) and a row in `agent/docs/TRYED.md`.

Report back: branch name and commits; what the audit of the existing `llm` strategy found against each spec point; what you built; the sandbox numbers per run (tactical vs yours), fallback count, measured LLM cost and seconds per message; any failure you could not fix; and your honest read of whether the evidence justifies a practice pass (the user's bar: no zeros or walk-aways and a mean at least tactical's, with gains in several cases, not one).

Промежуточный итог, пока два агента ещё работают (таймауты P05 + статистика по «final»; LLM-обёртка). Когда они вернутся, я волью починку таймаутов и сделаю финальный полный прогон.

## Что сделано

**P02 починен.** Штраф (relationship charge) вообще не попадал в наш расчёт: код ждал условия оплаты поставщика из PDF, а там их нет. Теперь они берутся из мастер-данных, себестоимость — 0.98 от should-cost «своего завода». Записанные ареной штрафы воспроизводятся с точностью до 56 €; сделок хуже стартовой цены за 32 сессии не было.

**Главный вывод по stabilise-кейсам:** цель — цена, минимизирующая C вместе со штрафом, а не цена, где штраф начинается. На P01 `c_best` арены совпадает с этим минимумом до цента.

**Твоя идея «просить меньше, чем готовы взять» сработала**, но в ограниченном виде. Под штрафом у каждой стоимости две цены; первые запросы идут по нижней. Каждый наш шаг вверх виден поставщику как уступка и нам ничего не стоит. Если он согласится сразу, теряем не больше четверти диапазона.

|---|---|---|---|
| P01 | 0.856 | 0.969 (последний прогон 0.952) | глубокий первый запрос, мелкие шаги |
| P02 | 0.686 | 0.733 | индексная оговорка по цене нашего минимума |
| P03 | 0.905 | 0.923 | should-cost как аргумент |
| P07 | 0.721 | 0.740 | первый запрос не глубже 13 % в routine |
| P11 | 0.545 | 0.672 | не разделено с изменениями в main |
| P18 | 0.419 | 0.618 | не разделено с изменениями в main |
| P08 | 0.570 | 0.550 | — |
| P04, P05, P10 | 0.860 / 0.742 / 0.647 | без изменений | — |

Полный прогон кандидата (коммит `7143676`): среднее 0.736 против 0.695, 10 из 10 сделок, без нулей и уходов. P07 и P03 улучшены уже после него, полного прогона на последнем коммите ещё нет. После правки ранжирования should-cost P01 не переигрывался — жду, что вернётся 0.969, проверит финальный прогон.

**Не сработало** (откатил, записал):
- жалобы по качеству как отдельные аргументы на P11 — арена вернула `duplicate`;
- довод «металл уже в цене по пункту 3.2 договора» на P08/P18 — арена не распознала его как аргумент, P18 упал до 0.485.

**Блеф «у нас есть альтернативы» не делал.** На sandbox жёсткий тон с такой фразой дал 0.614 против 0.736: поставщик просит показать данные и раньше ставит final. Не раскрывать лимит и держать нейтральный тон — уже так.

**Тест на аугментированных брифах:** 100 вариантов, только шаг разбора. Нашёл и я починил: `C_open` был бесконечным, когда единственная котировка нарушает must-have (P10, P11); страж вырезал все листы при must-have на нестандартном поле; падения на `parts: null` и `round_limit: null`. Неизвестный тип или цель кейса не роняют агента.

Потрачено 32 из 50. План на остаток: финальный полный прогон (10) после вливания починки таймаутов, 8 в резерве. Второй полный прогон считаю малополезным: без LLM на одинаковые письма приходят одинаковые ответы (P02 дал 0.733 три раза подряд).

| 08:00 | Load the Sunday data release: `negotiator data` | David | release files present, `negotiator health` ok |

| 11:00 | Final checks: `NEGOTIATOR_FINAL=1`, key, `negotiator me`, no open sessions; read `agent/docs/knowledge/competitions-info.md` | David | checklist ticked |
| 12:00 | `NEGOTIATOR_FINAL=1 negotiator final` (5 waves × 8 min, hidden cases, one try each) | David | every wave closed |

During the final the agent must not read `/v1/events`, `/screen`, `/leaderboard`, `/results`. Do not change code
between waves.

1. **`alt_structure` without its price rule** (menu part only): the structure of the supplier's alternative goes into
   our next menu, but its price is still only taken on its own end signal. Expectation: keeps P10's +0.078 (0.679)

87:`--strategy tactical-llm` runs `tactical` unchanged and lets a model reword the text of its ordinary offer e-mails
88-(`writer.py`): the reason, one question, the tone of the case goal. The sheets, the cited IDs, hold and accept stay

91-letter for letter, nothing about our limit or hurry, no threat, no promise, no claim without a source. A failed check,
92:an error or a slow call sends tactical's template. `tactical-llm+reader` adds a model reading of each reply
93-(`reader.py`) that may only add a requested lever the regular expressions missed.

Сравнение на sandbox сделано и лимит проверен; practice-попытку система разрешений не пропустила — нужен твой явный ответ по конкретной команде (ниже).

## Что измерено (sandbox, D01 + D02, haiku через CLI)

| | tactical | tactical-llm, лимит 10 с | tactical-llm, лимит 40 с |
|---|---|---|---|
| D01 / D02 | 0.649 / 0.587 | 0.649 / 0.587 | 0.649 / 0.587 |
| вызовов writer | — | 9 | 9 |
| текст модели ушёл поставщику | — | 0 | 8 |
| откат по таймауту | — | 8 | 0 |
| откат по валидатору | — | 1 | 1 |
| время на сообщение: среднее / макс. | — | 8.0 / 8.75 с | 11.4 / 14.5 с |

- **Жёсткий лимит работает.** При 10 с ни одно сообщение не вышло за лимит, каждый раз ушёл шаблон tactical.
- **Бага в проверке не вижу.** Валидатор срезал 1 текст из 9; остальные 8 откатов при лимите 10 с — таймауты.
- **Медленно из-за провайдера, а не модели.** `claude-code:haiku` запускает процесс CLI на каждый вызов: в среднем 11 с на письмо, максимум 14 с. Прямой API уложился бы в 10 с, но ключа для него в `.env` нет.
- **На sandbox формулировки LLM ничего не дали.** С 8 переписанными письмами из 9 счёт совпал с tactical до цента.
- **По умолчанию теперь 10 с** на сообщение, 8 с на writer, 4 с на reader — ветка `feat/llm-limit` (`3fbf436`), запушена, в main не влита. С текущим провайдером это означает «LLM никогда не успевает»; рабочее значение для него — 20 с.

## Отдельная находка: D01 на main упал

Обычный `tactical` на main даёт D01 0.649. На ветке до слияния с main было 0.769–0.809, вечером на старом коде — 0.969. Сейчас после первого ответа поставщика (51.30) агент заново ставит якорь на 46.17, поставщик не двигается, и мы берём 51.30. На ветке до слияния этого шага не было. D01 — stabilise-кейс без should-cost; закрытые кейсы такого типа поведут себя так же. Стоит разобрать до заморозки.

## Нужно твоё «да» на practice

Лимит 10 с дал бы точную копию tactical, поэтому предлагаю 20 с:

`LLM_MESSAGE_BUDGET_S=20 WRITER_TIMEOUT_S=18 uv run negotiator run --set practice --cases case:P01 case:P02 case:P03 case:P07 case:P08 case:P10 case:P11 case:P18 --strategy tactical-llm --llm claude-code:haiku --parallel 4`

- 8 сессий: без P05 (три поставщика и непочиненные таймауты) и P04 (потолок).
- Это весь остаток разрешённых 50 (потрачено 42). Баланс команды перед запуском не перечитывал (последнее виденное — 367 из 650), сброс 2026-10-11 12:47 UTC.
- Код запушен, коммит `3fbf436`.

Запускать так, или только один-два кейса (например P11 и P08 — 2 сессии)?
